items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: It was shortly before Bud Powell died in Paris.

ctx.x: First of all, we have tourists coming up here that ask, roll your window down, “Is there any hippies around?” Just to answer what you asked before. Okay. Ornette invented the harmolodic approach to music and I think he helped us all to be confident in our need to really express ourselves freely. Where it goes from there, I wouldn’t know. For me, Ornette is the final, at the moment. Where it would go from there, I wouldn’t know. Because he is the most, that’s the most natural music to me. Ornette’s personal…

painting, music. Because my older brother was also — he brought me actually to my first jazz concert and he always painted with music, you know. He had records and it was his biggest inspiration. And then I got my own agent and I wanted to do jazz and I went into the whole standards thing. And then about three years later after I did it alone, I met Karl and then we wanted to just build something up together. He played piano in the band I worked in and then one day he came home and said, “I think I found what we…
